issue_context.title: [Crypto] Implement Binance Bitcoin Exchange
issue_context.body:
Seeking a complete, tested [Binance](https://www.binance.com) bitcoin exchange implementation for QuantConnect, including the IDQH implementation for streaming binance data.  

1 - IBrokerage interface implementation for Binance. All IBrokerage tests should pass.
2 - IQueueDataHandler interface implementation for Binance streaming data.
3 - If possible IDataDownloader implementation for Lean/ToolBox for Binance API.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)

That's great news @Adalyat. For Binance support, are you using direct REST API calls or using any libraries?

Also I noticed there is this post [here](https://www.quantconnect.com/forum/discussion/4423/binance-crypto-trading-module) that a user says he has added Binance support to QuantConnect and operating. Maybe you can get a code review from him too.

I came across this project [ccxt-rest](https://ccxt-rest.io/) a few days ago. It's basically one REST interface to 135+ cryptocurrency exchanges. If we can add it as a broker to QuantConnect we can use all those exchanges.

#3511 

There is a [CCXT C# .NET wrapper](https://github.com/lisa3907/ccxt.net) implementation, of the original [CCXT](https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt), that supports hundreds of exchanges.
It would be interesting to incorporate in Lean, as @omidkrad said.

@joao-neves95 I reviewed the CCXT C# project that you referenced and it seems to be a reimplementation of CCXT rather than a wrapper. It supports only 26 exchanges and doesn't seem to be maintained that well, so I wouldn't recommend it. That said, it is possible to create a C# wrapper over CCXT using [Edge.js](https://github.com/tjanczuk/edge) by running CCXT in Node and exposing its functions in-process to .NET, however, I prefer a microservice approach with [ccxt-rest](https://ccxt-rest.io/).

I've created a separate issue for that https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues/3793

review_comments: I wonder if we need this static data to be resolved on application start and/or periodically for long-running live algorithms

Is there a way to resolve this information on launch, otherwise we'll always be out of date with supported symbols. Also, in some cases, symbols might not be the same on different exchanges. For example, there's multiple tokens that trade under the ticker `HOT` -- this shouldn't cause issues when running a single brokerage, but can potentially cause SID collisions.
Not really. We discussed it months ago and this feature isn't implemented yet. It would be nice to have a separate class to fetch all up-to-date static data on init.

I think the real issue is that it is **not** static data. Crypto exchanges are notorious for adding/removing symbols quite frequently. So if we're running a live algorithm we'll need this data to (potentially) produce symbol delisted events and maybe (eventually) an IPO-like event (symbol listed?) I'm happy to keep this as static data as a first revision solution, but we'll need to come up with a good pattern for managing the additions/removals from crypto exchanges.

Perhaps outside the scope of this PR, but it would be nice to have an `OrderBookCollection` or `OrderBookManager` of sorts as a self-contained component. Often times, such is the case with binance,  you can bind to their L2 data feed _without_ credentials. This could allow an algorithm trading on, for example, coinbase, to still get the binance quote books for usage within the algorithm.
If this is the desired retry request behavior, it might make sense to extract into it's own type so other types can benefit from it.

style - I never was a fan of the partial class pattern for brokerages. My preference would be to see multiple smaller classes instead of a single master class. The partial class pattern has been used in others, so we don't _need_ to change this as it matches existing patterns, but I do think it's worthwhile thinking about whether or not it's the best pattern. I could see what is currently a single brokerage being split into (for example) a `BinanceApiClient` to manage the request/response between lean and binance and a `BinanceBrokerage` that would use the `BinanceApiClient` as an adapter for the `IBrokerage` interface. This provides a nice separation of concerns and makes other components available for reuse.
Also, it's most likely the case that we don't need to lock the stream over the _entire_ method body, but only the sections that are sensitive to the stream being locked.
outside the scope of this PR, but I think for encapsulation purposes it makes sense for `UpdateAskRow` to perform the `quantity == 0` check internally to guarantee its own state is consistent.
Yeah. But might be supplied as separate PR. It's necessary for Binance as it uses USDT as account currency. But for now I've commented it out to attract additional attention :)

Attention attracted indeed!

This requires broader support for non-USD account currencies to be properly implemented.
@Adalyat I think we need broader non-USD support as a separate PR as a precursor to this one. Let's connect offline to discuss the work involved for that distinct PR.
